title: Nonlinear quantum noise polarization in macroscopic nonlinear QED
abstract: We construct a quantum theory of light in nonlinearly responding materials with dispersion and absorption and, in particular, show the emergence of non-Gaussian noise associated with nonlinear absorption processes. Our theory is based on a path-integral formulation of the microscopic Huttner-Barnett model including cubic matter self-interaction required for $χ^{(2)}$ nonlinear processes. We show that the noise polarization emerges naturally from a decoupling of the stochastic weights of the bath response which, in case of cubic self-interactions, leads to a decoupling via Airy functions. As the theory is, by construction, consistent with the nonlinear fluctuation-dissipation theorem, it constitutes a viable quantum theory of light in nonlinear media.

bite.hook: A new macroscopic QED framework shows nonlinear absorption produces inherently non-Gaussian quantum noise.
tldr: Constructed a macroscopic quantum electrodynamics theory for light traveling through nonlinear, absorbing media.
Formulated a path-integral extension of the microscopic Huttner-Barnett model with cubic matter interactions.
Discovered that nonlinear absorption decouples bath noise via Airy functions, generating non-Gaussian quantum noise.
bite.whyItMatters: Understanding how quantum noise behaves in complex optical materials is vital for designing high-fidelity quantum computers and non-classical light sources.
bite.eli5: Normally, background quantum fuzziness is shaped like a smooth bell curve. In materials that twist light nonlinearly, the noise gets distorted and skewed into a weird, non-bell-curve pattern.
